sections.h2: Who sends and collects Gordon County property tax bills?
sections.html:
The elected Tax Commissioner does both jobs. According to the county's office page, that office mails roughly 28,000 property tax bills a year and collects the county, county Board of Education and state property taxes. It also takes exemption applications, issues executions against delinquent taxpayers and sells vehicle tags.

The office is on the first floor of Government Plaza, 215 North Wall Street, Calhoun, GA 30701, phone 706-629-9242, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 5 pm. Mail payments go to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703, and a self-addressed stamped envelope brings back a receipt.

sections.h2: What makes Gordon County different for a house seller?
sections.html:
Gordon County is in northwest Georgia, with Calhoun as the county seat. The General Assembly created it on February 13, 1850 from parts of Cass (later Bartow) and Floyd counties, on land that had been Cherokee territory and included New Echota, the last seat of the Cherokee Nation. Cities are Calhoun, Fairmount and Plainville, and Resaca is a town. Wikipedia counts 358 square miles, almost all of it land.

Interstate 75 runs through the middle, and the county has more interstate exits than any other Georgia county. US 41, US 411 and several state routes cross it. Manufacturing anchors the economy: Mohawk Industries, the flooring maker, is headquartered here, and Shaw Industries, Beaulieu, LG Chem and Kobelco Construction Machinery America have a presence too.

The Census Bureau puts the July 2025 population at 61,701, up 7.2 percent from the 2020 base. There are 24,859 housing units, owners live in 73.9 percent of occupied homes, and the survey median owner value is $222,900. That figure is below the other two counties in the same QuickFacts table. Median household income is $63,650, and the average commute is 25.3 minutes. Builders took out 289 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: When are Gordon County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
The county's October 20, 2026 administrator report said the state tax digest and collection order were due from the Department of Revenue that day. It said bills would go out before October 31 and would be due on or before December 31. State law sets a default due date of December 20 and lets a county adopt another, so the date printed on your bill is the one that counts.

sections.h2: How do Gordon County tax payments and balances work?
sections.html:
Online payment goes through the county's tax payment site, which asks you to accept a disclaimer first. A credit card payment carries a 2.50 percent convenience fee charged by the processor, not by the county. Owners who want to skip it can mail a check to the post office box above. For delinquent bills more than seven years old, the page tells owners to contact the tax commissioner's office directly.

The same disclaimer gives closing attorneys and staff an instruction worth following: a property may be under appeal even when the website does not show it, so call 706-629-9242 for the most accurate balance before closing. The county offers no warranty on the website's figures.

sections.h2: What can a Gordon County owner do about the assessed value?
sections.html:
Use the yearly assessment notice. The state's guidance says the notice must explain how to appeal, and an appeal of fair market value goes to the board of tax assessors with a postmark no later than 45 days after the notice date. The county bills about 28,000 properties, so an owner who thinks the value is high is one of many reviewing the same notice.

  • Keep the notice envelope, because the mailing date starts the clock.
  • Collect sales of similar houses near yours and any repair estimates.
  • Ask the assessors' office which forms and evidence it prefers.
  • Ask the tax commissioner how an appealed parcel appears on the bill before you pay.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and filing dates matter in Gordon County?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner receives exemption applications, and state law lets an owner apply after the home becomes a primary residence, up to April 1 of the first year the exemption is wanted. Not applying is treated as a waiver. Property tax returns are filed between January 1 and April 1, and a person who returned or paid last year and then skips the return is deemed to have filed at last year's final value.

The Georgia revenue department also says municipalities levy their own tax, billed by the city clerk unless the city and county combined billing. Calhoun, Fairmount, Plainville and Resaca residents should ask which bills they will receive. Calhoun also runs its own city school system, with Calhoun Primary, Elementary, Middle and High Schools, so a house inside the city sits in a different school district from one in the county system. Ask the tax commissioner which school levy applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: How does Georgia treat unpaid Gordon County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
After the 60 days that follow a bill's postmark, interest can accrue, and penalties may be added to unpaid balances. The tax commissioner issues executions against delinquent taxpayers, and a recorded execution sits on the title until it is paid. A refund of tax that was wrongly assessed or collected must be requested within three years of payment.

A seller with a balance should ask for the payoff in writing, give it to the closing attorney, and expect the title company to pay it from the proceeds. We buy Gordon County houses as-is for cash, including homes in Calhoun and the smaller towns along I-75 where an owner has older repairs, tenants or back taxes. A cash buyer still needs a clear title, so the payoff is handled the same way. If an heir received the house under a recorded beneficiary deed, our Georgia transfer on death page lists what must be recorded before a sale.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Gordon County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay online through the county's tax payment site, or mail a check to GCTC, P. O. Box 337, Calhoun, GA 30703. The office is at 215 North Wall Street in Calhoun and takes calls at 706-629-9242.

faqs.q: How much did Gordon County lower its tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county reported a 7.7 mill rate for 2026, down from 9.042 mills in 2024 and 2025. Its report says the last lower rate was in 2002.

faqs.q: Is there a fee for paying by card in Gordon County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county page lists a 2.50 percent convenience fee on credit card transactions, charged by the processor. A mailed check avoids it.

faqs.q: Who can tell a closing attorney the real balance on a Gordon County parcel?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner's office, at 706-629-9242. The county warns that a parcel may be under appeal without the website showing it.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply for a homestead exemption in Georgia?
faqs.a: The state allows an application through April 1 of the first year the exemption is sought. Failure to apply is treated as a waiver, and the Gordon County tax commissioner receives the applications.
